content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on a project where a [product_name] is used as a client for Modbus communication. Is there a way to switch between Big Endian and Little Endian formats, or at least a method to swap the data order? Also, I'd like to know how to view the complete bit frame in the data table—when I read a 2-word register, only 16 bits are visible. I might be missing something, so any assistance is appreciated! Thank you in advance!

The [product_name] follows big endian format, and this setting can't be changed directly. You'll need to manually rearrange bytes or words since there isn't a built-in function block for swapping them. In the data table, make sure to choose the appropriate data type (like VD) and select the correct data format to see 32-bit values displayed as their full bit patterns.
Can you explain how to do that?
To clarify, are you looking to swap bytes or words?
Check the attachment for more details.
That's a creative solution—thanks a lot!

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced challenges with byte order adjustment in Modbus communication due to fixed endianness on [product_name]. Direct switching between big and little endian isn't available, so manual data reordering is necessary. Users also found it difficult to display complete bit frames for multi-word registers in the related data table interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hoped for an option or easy method to adjust endianness (byte/word order) and a clear way to view full bit frames for multi-word registers in the data table.
